This would have two main benefits, first and foremost, in most cases is easy to see if a post contributes to a discussion or not (using criteria as "it stays on topic", "present logical arguments" or "cites sources"), so it could follow that downvoating a post that contributes to the discussion carried a penalty (warnings and bans for repeated offenders)

The second benefit would be that, by ranking posts by up/downvoats and agree/disagree votes (giving greater wheight to up/downvoats) and hiding comments only by up/downvoats you could end with top comments that are not aligned with the current mayority view, furthering debate and constructive discussion, and diminishing the echo chamber effect.

aww, you guys. I always see managing a subverse as a partnership between moderators and community. Mods aren't just janitors, but they're definitely not police either. A mods' job is to help the community be what it wants to be, which is purely a support role. /v/gaming is a great community, very welcoming to newcomers, less focused on memes and joke content than Reddit's equivalent, and excels at deep, meaningful discussion. These are things that the community values, so a moderator's job is to listen to the community, support its wishes as accurately and transparently as possible, and manage the handful of specialized things that the community doesn't have the tools for directly. Most of the reason /v/gaming has been so drama-free is because it's got such an easygoing community, which makes moderating easy.
